summary: Develop carbon project baselines, MRV plans, and validation evidence. Explore the five-day intermediate course and review the curriculum.
lede: Carbon credit project certification involves documenting a mitigation activity, quantifying its emissions reductions or removals, and preparing evidence for assessment. For project developers, carbon programme staff, and sustainability professionals, this training covers project screening, boundaries, methodology selection, baseline and additionality analysis, quantification, monitoring plans, and organizing records for validation and verification.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who assess, develop, monitor, or review carbon credit projects and need to turn project concepts into documented, assessable proposals. This course is designed for: Carbon Project Developers preparing project design documents and methodology submissions. Carbon Programme Officers coordinating project registration and crediting-cycle requirements. Carbon Project Managers overseeing implementation, monitoring, and evidence collection. GHG Accountants quantifying project baselines and emissions reductions. MRV Specialists designing monitoring plans and data-quality controls. Carbon Project Analysts assessing additionality, leakage, and project feasibility. Land-Use Project Officers documenting carbon pools, boundaries, and permanence risks. Renewable Energy Project Developers calculating project emissions reductions against baselines. Validation and Verification Coordinators organizing evidence for independent assessment. Sustainability and Climate Finance Advisers screening carbon project quality and investment readiness.
modules: Project Boundaries + GHG Protocol Project Accounting
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with greenhouse gas accounting, climate mitigation projects, or sustainability reporting is recommended. No programming is required. You will use spreadsheet-based calculations; advanced remote-sensing and AI applications are introduced at a conceptual awareness level, not as implementation labs.
